On a miss: the guard answers “Never seen you before. Unless one of that lot will speak for you.”, at `speak`; the guard notes `turned-away` about the speaker alone, if the guard sees the speaker; so does each other carrier of `front-gate` the line's words reached and who is up, about the same members, whether or not that carrier sees them (heard); if the guard notes it about nobody, nobody else notes anything.

The speaker can say the line “They’re with us. The captain let us in.” (`vouch`) to the carrier. It is said at `speak` (the default): its words reach everyone in the speaker's room (the wall partition the speaker stands in), and anyone in the next room within 30 feet of the speaker by the way through an open doorway (a closed door stops them), and whoever it is said to, wherever they stand. Whoever sees the speaker is told who said it; whoever the words reach and does not see the speaker hears the words — and which line it was, the roll, whether it worked and what it taught — from someone unnamed; whoever only sees it said learns neither the words, which line it was, whether it worked, nor what it taught; whoever the words do not reach may still notice a voice by passive Perception, never a whisper; the one it is said to is named only to those who see them. It is a plain line: it rolls nothing, cannot be missed, and costs nothing on either clock.
